label: US 9th Cir. — Patel v Facebook (BIPA standing)
body: Holding: Facebook's "Tag Suggestions" facial-recognition feature — scanning user-uploaded photos to extract face templates without prior written consent or a publicly available retention schedule — violated BIPA Sec. 15(a) and 15(b). The Ninth Circuit held the violations created concrete and particularised harm sufficient for Article III standing — biometric privacy interests are substantive, not procedural.
Outcome: Class certified; settled for $650M in 2021 (originally $550M; raised on remand).

Why it matters: Established that BIPA's notice-and-consent provisions create concrete injury independent of pecuniary loss. Distinguishes BIPA-style biometric claims from the bare-procedural-violation analysis of Spokeo.
